Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 3

Strings in C are arrays of bytes
 A string ends with a zero byte, the null terminator
 strlen counts the bytes before the terminator
 strcpy copies bytes until it copies the terminator
 Pointer arithmetic moves through the array one byte at a time
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 4

ASCII uses seven bits per character
 A is 65, a is 97, the digit 0 is 48
 One byte holds one ASCII character, with room to spare
 Most of the world's writing does not fit in 128 characters
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 5

Unicode gives every character a code point
 A code point is just a number, written U+0041 for A
 The euro sign is U+20AC and a smiley is U+1F600
 UTF-8 is one way to encode code points as bytes
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 6

UTF-8 encoding of bytes
 1 byte:  0xxxxxxx
 2 bytes: 110xxxxx 10xxxxxx
 3 bytes: 1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
 4 bytes: 11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx
 How many bytes does a UTF-8 character use? Look at the first byte.
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 7

Bitwise operators in C
 & and, | or, ^ xor, ~ not
 << shifts bits left, >> shifts bits right
 x & 0xFF keeps the lowest eight bits
 x | 0x80 sets the top bit of a byte
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 8

Masks
 A mask picks out the bits you care about
 Use & with a mask to read bits, | to set bits, & ~mask to clear bits
 Example: (x >> 4) & 0xF reads the second hex digit
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 9

Printing bits
 for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--) { printf("%d", (b >> i) & 1); }
 Walk from the highest bit to the lowest
 Shift the bit you want down to position zero, then mask it
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 10

Counting characters, not bytes
 strlen("cafe") is 4, strlen of the accented word is 5
 To count code points, skip bytes that start with 10
 Continuation bytes never begin a character
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 11

Decoding a character
 Read the first byte and count its leading ones
 Strip the length marker with a mask
 Shift in six bits from each continuation byte
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 12

Common mistakes
 Using signed char and getting sign extension
 Forgetting that the shift of a negative number is not portable
 Writing past the end of the buffer when copying
Lecture 2 - Bits, Bytes and UTF-8 Text 13

Summary
 Strings are bytes, characters are code points
 UTF-8 stores code points in one to four bytes
 Bit operators let you build and take apart those bytes
 Next time: memory, malloc and free
